elasticstack_fleet_agent_download_source.reason: Real user-configurable feature (authenticating to a private download host with api_key, basic auth, or custom headers); the resource has no auth support today and no opaque attribute covers it, so this should be exposed.

Real user-configurable feature letting auth/ssl material for a download source be stored as a Fleet secret instead of plaintext; no opaque attribute or existing field covers this, so it should be exposed.

Real user-configurable feature (custom certificate/CA/key for a download host using self-signed or private certs); the resource has no SSL support today and no opaque attribute covers it, so this should be exposed.

elasticstack_fleet_agent_policy#/compone.reason: The advanced_settings block already mirrors most of this API sub-object (logging, download, go_max_procs, monitoring_runtime_experimental); these remaining agent feature toggles are a natural, low-risk extension of an attribute the resource already partially exposes, not computed or imperative fields.

elasticstack_fleet_custom_integration#/p.reason: List-catalog filter for browsing by category; irrelevant once a package is identified by exact name+version.
List-catalog filter for UI browsing by install status; not meaningful when the resource already targets a specific name+version.
Server-computed display count of package policies; purely informational and unrelated to resource configuration.
Only toggles inclusion of optional descriptive/display metadata (readme, screenshots, assets) in the read response; none of that data is surfaced by this resource.

Custom integrations are locally uploaded, EPR-unverified packages; the read step calls GetPackage without ignoreUnverified, so Kibana can reject reads for genuinely unsigned custom packages. Worth exposing so users can opt into tolerating unverified signatures on read.
